questions.q: The distinguishing feature of the Spiral model compared with other process models is
options: Explicit risk analysis in every iteration
questions.exp: Each loop of the Spiral model includes risk identification and resolution, making it risk-driven.

questions.q: A program flow graph has 14 edges and 11 nodes and is a single connected graph. What is its cyclomatic complexity V(G)?
Which of the following activities is an example of preventive maintenance?
options: Restructuring and refactoring code to reduce future maintenance problems
Fixing a crash reported by a user
Porting the software to a new operating system
Adding a new report requested by the client
questions.exp: Preventive maintenance improves the internal structure (e.g., refactoring) to avoid future problems; the other options are corrective, adaptive and perfective.

questions.q: The Singleton design pattern is used to:
options: create objects without specifying their exact class
add behaviour to an object dynamically
ensure a class has only one instance with a global access point
questions.exp: Singleton is a creational pattern restricting a class to one instance. Factory creates objects without naming the class, Decorator adds behaviour, Observer notifies dependents.

questions.q: In basic COCOMO, the exponent b in E = a x (KLOC)^b for an embedded project is:
questions.exp: Basic COCOMO constants: organic (2.4, 1.05), semi-detached (3.0, 1.12), embedded (3.6, 1.20). 0.38 is the organic time exponent d.

questions.q: Which technique describes requirements as sequences of interactions between a user and the system?
questions.exp: A use case captures the dialogue between an actor and the system to achieve a goal.

questions.q: A field accepts an integer age from 18 to 60. Which set of test values best represents boundary value analysis?
questions.exp: BVA tests values at and immediately around each boundary: 17, 18, 19 and 59, 60, 61.

questions.q: To unit test a module that calls other modules which are not yet developed, the tester uses:
questions.exp: A stub is a dummy called module. A driver is a dummy calling module, used when the caller is missing.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five information-domain components counted in Function Point Analysis?
questions.exp: FP counts external inputs, external outputs, external inquiries, internal logical files and external interface files. Number of classes is an object-oriented size measure.

questions.q: The cost of fixing a defect is generally lowest when the defect is detected during:
questions.exp: The relative cost of correcting an error rises steeply with each later phase, so early reviews and inspections are the most economical.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a desirable characteristic of a good Software Requirements Specification (SRS)?
options: Containing detailed implementation and coding decisions
questions.exp: An SRS should state what the system must do, not how it is implemented; embedding design/coding decisions is undesirable.

questions.q: In the SEI Capability Maturity Model (CMM), which maturity level is known as the 'Defined' level?
questions.exp: CMM levels are 1 Initial, 2 Repeatable, 3 Defined, 4 Managed, 5 Optimizing.

questions.q: A team spends 20 person-months at a cost of Rs 50,000 per person-month and produces 10,000 LOC. The cost per LOC is
In the Critical Path Method (CPM) of project scheduling, the critical path is
options: The shortest path from start to end
The longest path from start to end of the activity network
The path having the largest number of activities
The path having the maximum slack
questions.exp: The critical path is the longest duration path; it has zero slack and determines the minimum project duration.

questions.q: In throw-away (rapid) prototyping, the prototype is:
options: discarded after the requirements have been clarified
questions.exp: The throw-away prototype is built to elicit and validate requirements and is then discarded; the real system is built with proper design. Evolutionary prototyping instead refines the prototype into the product.

questions.q: Sandwich (hybrid) integration testing combines:
questions.exp: Sandwich testing integrates the top layers top-down with stubs while the lower layers are integrated bottom-up with drivers, meeting in the middle.

questions.q: A major disadvantage of using Lines of Code (LOC) as a size metric is that it:
options: depends on language and programming style and is known accurately only after coding
ignores the cost of the project
questions.exp: LOC varies with language and style, penalises concise code and is hard to estimate early; function points address this by measuring functionality.

questions.q: A risk has a probability of occurrence of 0.3 and the loss if it occurs is Rs 2,00,000. The risk exposure is
questions.exp: Risk exposure = probability × loss = 0.3 × 2,00,000 = Rs 60,000.

questions.q: In structured design, the fan-out of a module is
options: The number of modules directly called by it
The number of modules that call it
The number of lines of code it contains
The number of parameters passed to it
questions.exp: Fan-out counts subordinate modules invoked by a module; fan-in counts its callers.

questions.q: A project of 24 KLOC was completed in 48 person-months. The productivity in LOC per person-month is
questions.exp: Productivity = 24000 / 48 = 500 LOC per person-month.

questions.q: Which tool shows the hierarchy of modules and the calling relationship between them?
questions.exp: A structure chart depicts the modular hierarchy and the invocation relations among modules.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a CASE tool?
options: A code generator from design models
A spreadsheet-based payroll application used by the accounts department
questions.exp: CASE tools assist software development activities; a payroll application is an end-user application, not a development aid.

questions.q: The question 'Are we building the product right?' relates to
questions.exp: Verification checks conformance to specification (building the product right); validation asks whether we are building the right product.

questions.q: A static program analysis tool
options: Examines source code without executing it to detect potential defects
Executes the program with test data to measure statement coverage
Measures the response time of a running application under load
Automatically generates the graphical user interface
questions.exp: Static analysis inspects code (e.g., for uninitialized variables, unreachable code) without running it.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirements elicitation technique?
questions.exp: Code inspection is a verification activity on source code, not a technique for gathering requirements.

questions.q: The application-composition model of COCOMO II estimates size using:
questions.exp: COCOMO II application composition (used for prototyping and GUI-based projects) is based on object points; the early-design and post-architecture models use function points or SLOC.

questions.q: Which document serves as the formal description of what a software system is to do, agreed between customer and developer?
questions.exp: The SRS records the agreed functional and non-functional requirements of the system.

questions.q: In Boehm's spiral model diagram, the radial distance from the centre represents:
options: the cumulative cost incurred so far
the size of the development team
questions.exp: In the spiral model the radial dimension is cumulative cost to date, while the angular dimension represents progress through the quadrants of each cycle.

questions.q: Two modules communicate by reading and writing the same global data area. The type of coupling is
questions.exp: Sharing global data between modules is common coupling.

questions.q: A test coverage analyzer reports
options: The response time of the application
The number of concurrent users supported
The percentage of code elements executed by the test suite
The defect density of the module
questions.exp: Coverage tools instrument code and report which statements/branches were executed during testing.

questions.q: Testing performed by the customer to decide whether to accept the delivered system is called
questions.exp: Acceptance testing validates the system against user requirements and is used by the customer to accept or reject it.

questions.q: Tasks: A (3 days, no predecessor), B (5 days, after A), C (2 days, after A), D (4 days, after both B and C). The minimum project duration is
questions.exp: Longest path A→B→D = 3+5+4 = 12 days (A→C→D is only 9 days).

questions.q: Which of the following should NOT be included in a Software Requirements Specification?
options: Choice of algorithms and design/implementation details
questions.exp: An SRS states what the system must do, not how; design and implementation decisions belong to the design documents (IEEE 830).

questions.q: Software Quality Assurance (SQA) activities are applied
options: Only to the final source code
questions.exp: SQA is a process-wide umbrella activity covering reviews, standards, audits and testing at all phases.

questions.q: In UML, which diagram best shows the time-ordered sequence of messages exchanged between objects?
questions.exp: A sequence diagram arranges object interactions along a vertical time axis.

questions.q: In McCall's quality model, which of the following is a product transition factor?
questions.exp: Product transition: portability, reusability, interoperability. Product operation: correctness, reliability, efficiency, integrity, usability. Product revision: maintainability, flexibility, testability.

questions.q: A CASE tool that generates class skeleton code from a UML class diagram supports
questions.exp: Generating code from design models is forward engineering; extracting models from code is reverse engineering.

questions.q: Which type of cohesion is the strongest (most desirable)?
questions.exp: Functional cohesion, where all elements contribute to a single well-defined task, is the highest level of cohesion.

questions.q: Among the following white-box coverage criteria, which is the strongest?
questions.exp: Path coverage requires every independent execution path to be exercised and subsumes branch coverage, which in turn subsumes statement coverage.

questions.q: In the V-model of software development, acceptance testing is associated with which development phase?
questions.exp: In the V-model each development phase is paired with a test level; user requirements correspond to acceptance testing.

questions.q: Which UML diagram models the states of an object and the transitions triggered by events?
questions.exp: State machine diagrams show an object's states and event-driven transitions. Class diagrams show static structure; component and deployment diagrams show physical organisation.

questions.q: In a UML class diagram, a line with a filled (solid) diamond at one end represents
questions.exp: A filled diamond denotes composition (strong whole-part, part cannot exist without the whole); a hollow diamond denotes aggregation.

questions.q: A module has 45 defects found in 15 KLOC of code. The defect density is
questions.exp: Defect density = 45 / 15 = 3 defects per KLOC.

questions.q: In Scrum, who is primarily responsible for maximizing the value of the product and managing the product backlog?
questions.exp: The Product Owner owns and prioritizes the product backlog.

questions.q: Bottom-up integration testing requires the use of
questions.exp: In bottom-up integration, lower-level modules are tested first, so drivers are needed to simulate the higher-level callers.

questions.q: The prototyping model is most appropriate when
options: The requirements are completely known and frozen
The system is a purely computational batch program
The customer's requirements are unclear or incomplete
The project has no user interface
questions.exp: Prototypes help users and developers clarify vague or incomplete requirements through early feedback.

questions.q: Decision table testing is a technique of:
questions.exp: Decision table testing derives test cases from combinations of input conditions in the specification, without looking at code, so it is black-box.

questions.q: Which ISO/IEC standard defines the software life cycle processes?
questions.exp: ISO/IEC 12207 establishes a framework of processes for the software life cycle; the others deal with environment, security and food safety.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-functional requirement?
options: The system shall calculate income tax from the salary entered
The system shall allow users to search products by name
The system shall respond to any search query within 2 seconds
The system shall generate a monthly sales report
questions.exp: Response time is a performance constraint (quality attribute), hence non-functional; the others describe functions.

questions.q: A Gantt chart is mainly used to show
options: Project tasks as bars against a time scale
The flow of data between processes
The degree of coupling among modules
questions.exp: A Gantt chart plots task start, duration and finish as horizontal bars over a calendar.

questions.q: A project has an Unadjusted Function Point count of 125 and the sum of the 14 general system characteristic ratings is 30. Using FP = UFP × (0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi), the function point count is
The main purpose of regression testing is to
options: Test only the newly added feature
Measure system performance under heavy load
Verify that changes have not broken previously working functionality
questions.exp: Regression testing re-runs earlier tests after modification to catch unintended side effects.

questions.q: In basic COCOMO for an organic project, development time is D = 2.5 × E^0.38 months. For an effort E = 32 person-months, D is approximately
A system has MTTF = 400 hours and MTTR = 20 hours. Its availability is approximately
questions.exp: Availability = MTTF / (MTTF + MTTR) = 400/420 ≈ 0.952, i.e. about 95.2%.

questions.q: Using basic COCOMO for an organic project, effort E = 2.4 × (KLOC)^1.05 person-months. For a 10 KLOC project the effort is approximately
The IEEE 830 recommended practice deals with
questions.exp: IEEE Std 830 gives recommended practice for writing an SRS.

questions.q: Which combination of design characteristics makes software easiest to maintain?
options: Low coupling, high cohesion and good documentation
questions.exp: Loosely coupled, cohesive and well-documented modules localize changes and are easy to understand.

questions.q: A Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) is
options: A chart of the team's organization
A hierarchical decomposition of project work into smaller tasks and deliverables
A table of costs versus benefits
questions.exp: WBS breaks the project scope into manageable work packages in a tree structure.

questions.q: Statement I: The Waterfall model easily accommodates changes in requirements late in development. Statement II: Prototyping helps in clarifying requirements. Which is correct?
options: Statement I is false and Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
questions.exp: Waterfall is rigid and handles late change poorly, whereas prototypes elicit user feedback that clarifies requirements.

questions.q: In MoSCoW requirements prioritisation, the letter "W" stands for:
questions.exp: MoSCoW = Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time.

questions.q: Which SDLC model is most suitable when the requirements are clearly understood and fixed in advance, and each phase must be completed before the next one begins?
questions.exp: The Waterfall model is a linear sequential model that works best for stable, well-understood requirements.

questions.q: According to Lehman's laws of software evolution, a program used in a real-world environment must continually be adapted or it becomes progressively less useful. This is the law of
questions.exp: The law of Continuing Change states that E-type systems must be continually adapted to remain satisfactory.

questions.q: Which design pattern defines a one-to-many dependency so that when one object changes state all its dependents are notified automatically?
questions.exp: Observer is a behavioural pattern (publish-subscribe style). Singleton is creational; Adapter and Facade are structural.

questions.q: Brooks' law states that
options: Software complexity grows exponentially with lines of code
Project cost doubles with every new module
Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later
Every program contains at least one defect per 1000 lines
questions.exp: Brooks' law: adding people to a late project increases communication overhead and training effort, delaying it further.

questions.q: In a data flow diagram (DeMarco/Yourdon notation), a circle (bubble) represents a
questions.exp: A bubble denotes a process that transforms input data flows into output data flows.

questions.q: Statement I: 100% branch coverage guarantees 100% statement coverage (for code without unreachable statements). Statement II: 100% statement coverage guarantees 100% branch coverage. Which is correct?
options: Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
questions.exp: Executing every branch executes every statement, but executing every statement may still miss e.g. the false outcome of an if without else.

questions.q: In structured design, transform analysis and transaction analysis are used to convert:
options: a structure chart into source code
a data flow diagram into a structure chart
a use case into a class diagram
questions.exp: Structured analysis produces DFDs; transform or transaction analysis maps the DFD to a structure chart (module hierarchy), the main structured-design output.

questions.q: ISO 9001 is primarily concerned with
questions.exp: ISO 9001 specifies requirements for a quality management system.

questions.q: Match: 1 Corrective, 2 Adaptive, 3 Perfective, 4 Preventive with a) fixing defects, b) adjusting to a new operating system, c) adding requested features, d) restructuring to avoid future problems. Select the correct matching.
questions.exp: Corrective fixes faults, adaptive responds to environment change, perfective adds/enhances features, preventive restructures for future maintainability.

questions.q: In PERT, an activity has optimistic time 2 days, most likely time 5 days and pessimistic time 14 days. The expected time is
In the SOLID principles of object-oriented design, the Single Responsibility Principle says that:
options: a class should be open for extension but closed for modification
a class should have only one reason to change
subclasses must be replaceable for their base class
clients should not depend on interfaces they do not use
questions.exp: S = Single Responsibility (one reason to change). The other options describe Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution and Interface Segregation respectively.

questions.q: Which type of coupling between two modules is the most undesirable (highest degree of coupling)?
questions.exp: Content coupling, where one module directly modifies or relies on the internals of another, is the strongest and worst form of coupling.

questions.q: A program flow graph drawn as a planar graph has 6 regions (including the outer region). Its cyclomatic complexity is
questions.exp: V(G) equals the number of regions of the planar flow graph, so V(G) = 6.

questions.q: Mutation testing is used to
options: Evaluate the quality of a test suite by seeding small faults in the code
Convert black-box tests into white-box tests
questions.exp: Small mutations are introduced into the program; a good test suite should detect (kill) the mutants.

questions.q: According to the Agile Manifesto, which of the following is valued more?
options: Responding to change over following a plan
Following a plan over responding to change
Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
questions.exp: The manifesto values responding to change over following a plan, while acknowledging value in the items on the right.

questions.q: In Function Point Analysis, the Complexity Adjustment Factor (0.65 + 0.01 × ΣFi, with 14 factors each rated 0 to 5) has a maximum value of
Which of the following is a technique for requirements validation?
questions.exp: Requirements validation checks that the SRS reflects customer needs using reviews, walkthroughs, prototyping and test-case generation.

questions.q: Changing the internal structure of code to improve its readability and maintainability without changing its external behaviour is called
questions.exp: Refactoring restructures existing code while preserving its observable behaviour.

questions.q: In Six Sigma quality, the target defect level is approximately
questions.exp: Six Sigma aims at no more than 3.4 defects per million opportunities.

questions.q: Level 5 (Optimizing) of the CMM is characterised by
questions.exp: At the Optimizing level, quantitative feedback and innovative ideas drive continuous process improvement.
